questions.prompt: A C# call writes named arguments in reverse parameter order, and each expression logs a message. In what order are those expressions evaluated?

choices.text: In their written order in the argument list
In parameter declaration order, regardless of names
In alphabetical order of the named parameters
In reverse written order before binding to parameters

questions.explanation: Names control binding, not evaluation order. The expressions run in the order the caller writes them.

sources.title: Named and Optional Arguments
sources.claim: Argument expressions are evaluated in their written order, not parameter order; named arguments can supply a later optional parameter.

questions.prompt: A C# iterator opens a stream in a `using` declaration and yields lines. Its caller exits a `foreach` with `break`. What happens to that stream?

choices.text: It stays open until a full second enumeration completes
It closes at the first yield before the caller reads a line
It stays open until the garbage collector finalizes it
It is disposed as foreach disposes the enumerator

questions.explanation: foreach disposes its enumerator on early exit. That disposal executes iterator cleanup; yield suspension itself does not end the using lifetime.

sources.title: yield statement
sources.claim: Calling an iterator defers execution; using resources survive yield suspension and are disposed when enumeration completes or the enumerator is disposed.

questions.prompt: A C# service uses `catch (IOException ex) when (ShouldHandle(ex))`. Which behaviors hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A throwing filter is treated as evaluating to false
The filter is evaluated before stack unwinding
A false filter skips this catch and continues the search
The filter executes after this catch body has completed
A true filter suppresses execution of this catch body

questions.explanation: The filter participates in handler selection before unwinding. False skips the handler; true selects its body. If filter evaluation throws, that filter is treated as false rather than replacing the original exception.

sources.title: Exception-handling statements
sources.claim: A when filter is evaluated before stack unwinding; false skips the catch and a throwing filter is treated as false.

sources.title: Statements - C# language specification
sources.claim: If an exception filter throws, its evaluation is treated as false and handler search continues for the original exception.

questions.prompt: In C#, `Mark` logs its string argument and returns an integer, and `Write` declares parameters `(int first, int second)`. What is the log order for `Write(second: Mark("B"), first: Mark("A"))`?

choices.text: A then B, following the declared parameter order
A then B, following the named arguments alphabetically
B then A, following the written argument order
Either order, because named expressions are unordered

questions.explanation: The argument expressions execute in written order: Mark("B") before Mark("A"). Their values then bind to second and first respectively; parameter declaration order and alphabetical order do not control evaluation.

sources.title: Named and Optional Arguments
sources.claim: Argument expressions are evaluated in their written order, not parameter order; named arguments can supply a later optional parameter.

questions.prompt: A method returns `IEnumerable<string>` using `yield return`, and its body opens a file before yielding. When does the file-opening code first run?

choices.text: When the caller first advances the enumerator
When the iterator method returns its enumerable object
When the caller stores the enumerable in a local variable
When the compiler generates the iterator state machine

questions.explanation: An iterator call creates the deferred iteration machinery. Execution begins when enumeration advances, not when the enumerable is stored.

sources.title: yield statement
sources.claim: Calling an iterator defers execution; using resources survive yield suspension and are disposed when enumeration completes or the enumerator is disposed.

questions.prompt: A diagnostic filter logs an exception and returns false. Which statements describe this design? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The filter can inspect state before stack unwinding
This catch body executes before the search continues
False replaces the original exception with a new filter exception
The logging itself means the exception is now handled
The handler search continues past this catch clause

questions.explanation: Returning false declines this handler while retaining the original exception. Logging does not handle it, and this catch body never runs. The filter executes during the search before unwinding.

sources.title: Exception-handling statements
sources.claim: A when filter is evaluated before stack unwinding; false skips the catch and a throwing filter is treated as false.

sources.title: Statements - C# language specification
sources.claim: If an exception filter throws, its evaluation is treated as false and handler search continues for the original exception.
